name: Greece
tagline: Six thousand islands, of which two hundred and twenty-seven are inhabited, and a mainland almost nobody visits.
summary: Greece is more mountain than island by area, and the mainland — Epirus, the Pindus, the Peloponnese — is emptier and greener than the postcards suggest. The islands divide into groups with different architecture, food and weather; the Cyclades are white and windy, the Ionians green, the Dodecanese medieval. Everything closes down in the afternoon heat and reopens at six, which is not laziness but sense.

season.note: May, June, September and early October are the sweet spot: swimmable sea, open tavernas, tolerable ruins. August is the whole of Greece and half of Europe on the same ferries. Many island businesses close entirely from November to April.

getting_around: Ferries are the network: fast catamarans and slow open-deck boats, both booked online and both cancelled by wind. Domestic flights save a day to the far islands. The mainland needs a car; the Athens metro is excellent and has an archaeological museum inside a station.
food: Whatever is in the pot that day — ask to see the kitchen, which is normal
Greek salad with no lettuce, and bread to finish the oil
Wine from Santorini's assyrtiko and Naoussa's xinomavro, both serious and both cheap here

festivals.name: Orthodox Easter — the biggest event of the year
Athens & Epidaurus Festival, in ancient theatres

know: Ferry cancellations for wind are common and not negotiable; leave a buffer day before a flight home.
Many older buildings ask you to bin paper rather than flush it — follow the sign.
Archaeological sites close early in winter and midday shade is scarce; go at opening.

regions.name: Athens & the Peloponnese
regions.summary: The classical core: the Acropolis, Mycenae, Olympia and a peninsula of castles and empty coast.

cities.name: Athens
cities.summary: A sprawling modern capital with a 2,500-year-old temple on a rock in the middle and a food scene that got very good, quietly.
highlights: The Acropolis at opening, and the Acropolis Museum afterwards, in that order
The National Archaeological Museum, which is the real prize
Rooftop bars looking at a floodlit Parthenon
Anafiotika, a Cycladic village accidentally inside the city

experiences.name: The Acropolis Museum, third floor
experiences.summary: The Parthenon frieze laid out at actual scale and orientation, with plaster casts where the British Museum holds the originals — the gaps are the argument.

places.name: The Acropolis
places.summary: The Parthenon, the Erechtheion and the Propylaea on one rock, best at opening or in the last hour.

places.name: Acropolis Museum
places.summary: The Parthenon frieze laid out at actual scale and orientation, with casts where the originals are in London.

places.name: National Archaeological Museum
places.summary: The Mask of Agamemnon, the Antikythera mechanism, and the best classical collection anywhere.

places.name: Anafiotika
places.summary: A Cycladic village built inside Athens by island masons in the 1840s, and still lived in.

cities.name: Nafplio
cities.summary: Greece's first capital: Venetian, neoclassical, under two fortresses, on a gulf in the Peloponnese.
highlights: Palamidi fortress and its 999 steps
Epidaurus's theatre, where a coin dropped on stage is audible in the back row
Mycenae's lion gate, forty minutes north

experiences.name: The acoustics at Epidaurus
experiences.summary: Sit in the top row and have someone whisper on the orchestra floor. Built in the 4th century BC and still unexplained in full.

places.name: Palamidi
places.summary: A Venetian fortress of eight bastions above the town, reached by 999 steps or a road.

places.name: Epidaurus Theatre
places.summary: A 4th-century BC theatre whose acoustics carry a whisper to the back row, and still nobody fully knows why.

places.name: Mycenae
places.summary: The Lion Gate and the shaft graves of a civilisation that collapsed three thousand years ago.

cities.name: Monemvasia
cities.summary: A Byzantine town hidden on the seaward side of a rock island, invisible from the mainland.
highlights: A single gate, and no cars inside the walls
The upper town's ruins and Hagia Sophia on the summit
Swimming off the rocks below the walls

places.name: The Upper Town
places.summary: A Byzantine town on top of the rock, with Hagia Sophia on the edge and almost nobody up there.

cities.name: Delphi
cities.summary: The navel of the ancient world, on a terrace of Mount Parnassus above a sea of olive trees.
highlights: The sacred way up to the temple of Apollo, where the oracle spoke
The bronze Charioteer, which survived because an earthquake buried it
The stadium at the top, above everything, and usually empty

experiences.name: The sacred way at opening
experiences.summary: The site opens at eight and the coaches arrive at ten. Two hours of Delphi alone is a different place from Delphi at noon.

places.name: Sanctuary of Apollo
places.summary: The sacred way, the temple, the treasuries and the stadium above them all, on a terrace of Parnassus.

places.name: Delphi Museum
places.summary: The bronze Charioteer, which survived because an earthquake buried it.

cities.name: Olympia
cities.summary: Where the games were held every four years for a millennium, in a wooded valley between two rivers.
highlights: The original stadium, entered through its vaulted tunnel
The workshop of Pheidias, identified by a cup with his name on it
Hermes of Praxiteles in the museum, found where it fell

places.name: The Stadium
places.summary: Entered through a vaulted tunnel, with the original start line still in place.

cities.name: Mystras
cities.summary: A Byzantine city on a spur of Taygetos, abandoned in the 1950s and left standing: palaces, churches and frescoes.
highlights: A whole late-Byzantine city, walked from the castle down
Frescoes in six churches, most of them unrestored
Sparta below, which has almost nothing left

places.name: Mystras
places.summary: A whole late-Byzantine city on a spur of Taygetos: palaces, churches, frescoes, walked downhill.

cities.name: Kardamyli & the Mani
cities.summary: Stone tower houses on a wild peninsula where blood feuds ran into the 20th century, above a clear sea.
highlights: Tower villages built for feuding families, still standing empty
The Viros gorge, walked from the sea up into Taygetos
Patrick Leigh Fermor's house, now open by appointment

places.name: Viros Gorge
places.summary: A dry riverbed walked from the sea up into Taygetos, past chapels cut into the rock.

cities.name: Hydra
cities.summary: An island two hours from Athens with no cars and no bicycles at all — mules, boats and feet.
highlights: Shipowners' mansions round a stone harbour, from the 1790s
No wheeled traffic of any kind, by law
Swimming off the rocks at Spilia, straight from the town

places.name: Hydra Harbour
places.summary: Shipowners' stone mansions round a working port with no cars, no bicycles and mules on the quay.

regions.name: The Islands
regions.summary: Cyclades, Dodecanese, Ionian and Crete — related, and not remotely the same.

cities.name: Naxos
cities.summary: The largest Cycladic island: mountain villages, marble quarries, a working agricultural interior and long sandy beaches.
highlights: The Portara, a temple doorway on an islet at the harbour
Halki and the mountain villages, with citron distilleries
An unfinished 6th-century BC kouros lying in a field where it cracked

experiences.name: The interior, not the beach
experiences.summary: Half the island is farmland at altitude — cheese, potatoes and Venetian towers, twenty minutes from the sand.

places.name: Portara
places.summary: A temple doorway on an islet at the harbour, left standing because the marble was too big to steal.

places.name: The unfinished kouros
places.summary: A ten-metre marble figure lying where it cracked in the quarry 2,600 years ago.

cities.name: Santorini
cities.summary: The rim of a drowned volcano, with villages on the edge of a 300-metre cliff and vines grown in baskets on the ground.
highlights: Akrotiri: a Bronze Age town buried in ash and preserved whole
Assyrtiko from vines trained into wreaths against the wind
The caldera path from Fira to Oia — walked early, not at sunset

experiences.name: Vines grown in baskets
experiences.summary: No trellises: the vines are woven into circles on the ground to shelter the fruit from wind and catch night moisture.

places.name: Akrotiri
places.summary: A Bronze Age town buried in ash and preserved whole, with two-storey houses and drains that still work.

places.name: The caldera path
places.summary: Ten kilometres along the rim from Fira to Oia, walked early rather than at sunset.

cities.name: Chania, Crete
cities.summary: A Venetian harbour with an Ottoman quarter behind it, on an island large enough to be its own country.
highlights: The Venetian lighthouse and the harbour arc
Samaria gorge: 16 km down through the White Mountains to the sea
Cretan food — the diet the research is about — in mountain villages

experiences.name: Down the Samaria gorge
experiences.summary: Sixteen kilometres, one direction only, ending at a boat because there is no road out. Open May to October.

places.name: Samaria Gorge
places.summary: Sixteen kilometres downhill through the White Mountains to a village with no road out.

places.name: Venetian Harbour
places.summary: A curved quay, a lighthouse rebuilt by Egyptians in the 1830s, and a mosque at the near end.

cities.name: Rhodes
cities.summary: A walled medieval city built by crusader knights, on an island of Ottoman villages and butterfly valleys.
highlights: The largest inhabited medieval town in Europe, inside four kilometres of wall
Lindos's acropolis above a white village and a bay
Ottoman baths and mosques the guidebooks skip

places.name: Palace of the Grand Master
places.summary: A crusader fortress rebuilt by Italy in the 1930s as a holiday residence for Mussolini, who never used it.

places.name: Lindos Acropolis
places.summary: A Doric stoa on a rock above a white village and a bay, climbed on foot or by donkey.

cities.name: Milos
cities.summary: A volcanic island of white rock formations, coloured mining beaches and boat-only coves.
highlights: Sarakiniko: white pumice worn into a moonscape by the sea
Kleftiko's sea caves, reachable only by boat
Fishermen's syrmata: garages cut into the rock, painted, now let out

experiences.name: Round the island by boat
experiences.summary: Half the coast has no road to it. A day boat from Adamas is the only way to see Kleftiko and the southern coves.

places.name: Sarakiniko
places.summary: White pumice worn by the sea into something that looks like nowhere else in the Mediterranean.

places.name: Kleftiko
places.summary: Sea caves and stacks on a coast with no road to it, reached only by boat.

cities.name: Paros
cities.summary: Cycladic in the way people imagine the Cyclades, with marble quarries that supplied the ancient world and a working town behind the beaches.
highlights: Naoussa's small harbour, before the evening crowd
The Byzantine road, a marble path over the hills to Lefkes
Parian marble, which the Venus de Milo is made of

cities.name: Symi
cities.summary: Neoclassical mansions in ochre and blue stacked round a horseshoe harbour, an hour from Rhodes.
highlights: The harbour at Gialos, which is the reason to come
Panormitis monastery at the southern end, reached by boat
Sponge diving history, and the shops that still sell them

cities.name: Corfu
cities.summary: Venetian for four centuries and British for fifty, green all year, with an old town that looks nothing like the Aegean.
highlights: The UNESCO old town, Venetian streets and two fortresses
Cricket on the Spianada, a British hangover
Mount Pantokrator, and Albania visible across the strait

places.name: Old Fortress
places.summary: A Venetian fort on a rock islet, with a Georgian garrison church inside it.

cities.name: Kefalonia
cities.summary: The largest Ionian island: an underground lake, a mountain of black fir, and the loggerhead turtles offshore.
highlights: Melissani cave, where the roof collapsed and the light comes straight down
Mount Ainos, black fir found nowhere else
Robola wine, grown on limestone at altitude

cities.name: Ikaria
cities.summary: A steep island where people routinely live past ninety, festivals start at midnight and shops open when they open.
highlights: Panigiria: village festivals that run until dawn and are not for tourists
Radioactive hot springs at Therma, used since antiquity
Nas and the west coast, which is nearly roadless

experiences.name: A panigiri that ends at dawn
experiences.summary: A village saint's day: one long table, live violin and lute, dancing in a circle, and food priced to cover the church roof.

cities.name: Heraklion & Knossos
cities.summary: Crete's capital and the Minoan palace beside it — Europe's oldest city, and a reconstruction people still argue about.
highlights: Knossos, and Evans's concrete reconstructions, which are the argument
The archaeological museum, which holds what Knossos actually yielded
Venetian walls, and Kazantzakis buried on top of them

places.name: Knossos
places.summary: The Minoan palace, and Evans's concrete reconstructions, which are the argument as much as the site.

places.name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
places.summary: What Knossos actually yielded — the frescoes, the bull-leaping, the undeciphered discs.

regions.name: Northern Greece
regions.summary: Meteora's monasteries on rock pillars, Epirus's stone villages, and Thessaloniki's food.

cities.name: Meteora (Kalambaka)
cities.summary: Six working monasteries on top of sandstone pillars, reached for centuries by rope ladder and net.
highlights: The footpaths between monasteries, which almost every visitor drives instead
Frescoes inside Varlaam and Great Meteoron
Sunset from the rocks, not from the coach park

experiences.name: The old monks' paths
experiences.summary: Stone-cut trails link the pillars through the woods; three hours on foot beats a whole day by road.

places.name: Great Meteoron
places.summary: The largest of the six working monasteries, on the highest pillar, reached now by steps rather than net.

places.name: Varlaam
places.summary: Frescoed throughout, with the windlass tower that hauled everything up for four hundred years.

cities.name: Thessaloniki
cities.summary: Greece's second city: Byzantine, Ottoman and Sephardic layers, and the country's most confident food.
highlights: The Rotunda and the Byzantine churches on the UNESCO list
Modiano and Kapani markets, then bougatsa for breakfast
The waterfront walk to the Umbrellas at dusk

places.name: The Rotunda
places.summary: A 4th-century Roman rotunda that has been a mausoleum, a church and a mosque, and keeps its minaret.

places.name: Jewish Museum of Thessaloniki
places.summary: Four centuries of a majority-Sephardic city, and 1943, told without flinching.

cities.name: Zagori (Monodendri)
cities.summary: Forty-six stone villages in the Pindus mountains, linked by packhorse bridges over the deepest gorge in the world by ratio.
highlights: The Vikos gorge, from the Oxya viewpoint or from inside it
Arched stone bridges built by 18th-century merchant guilds
Bears, wolves and 1,800 plant species in the national park

places.name: Vikos Gorge
places.summary: The deepest gorge in the world by width-to-depth ratio, seen from Oxya or walked from inside.

places.name: The stone bridges
places.summary: Single- and triple-arched packhorse bridges built by 18th-century merchant guilds, still crossed on foot.

cities.name: Pelion (Makrinitsa)
cities.summary: Stone villages with slate roofs on a wooded mountain that drops to beaches on both sides.
highlights: Kalderimia: cobbled mule paths between villages, still the best way around
The narrow-gauge Moutzouris railway, built by Evaristo de Chirico
Apples, chestnuts and firs on one side of the ridge, the Aegean on the other

cities.name: Kavala
cities.summary: An Ottoman aqueduct over a harbour town, with Philippi's ruins inland and Thasos across the water.
highlights: The Kamares aqueduct, striding across the middle of town
Philippi: a Roman city, a battlefield, and where Paul first preached in Europe
Ferries to Thasos, which is green and largely undeveloped

cities.name: Ioannina
cities.summary: An Ottoman lake city with an island in it, a silversmithing tradition and the gateway to Zagori.
highlights: The walled kastro, and two mosques still standing inside it
The island, reached in ten minutes, with five monasteries and no cars
Silverwork, which the city has done for four centuries
